sources.note: Phonology is Tembé/Guajajára only. On Turiwára it says the available data 'consistem em uma reduzida lista de palavras' (quoting Figueiredo 2004, p. 104) and that Suruí and Turiwára have 'pouquíssimo material descrito'. No Turiwára stress.

sources.citation: Rodrigues, Aryon D. 1985. Relações internas na família lingüística Tupí-Guaraní. Revista de Antropologia 27/28: 33-53.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Comparative classification only. Turiwára is placed in subconjunto VIII (with Takunyapé, Wayampí, Emérillon, Amanayé, Anambé, Guajá, Urubú), defined by consonantal criteria (pp. 41-42); the accent criteria ('deslocamento do acento da última para a penúltima sílaba' for subconjuntos I-II, 'conservação do acento' for III) are not applied to VIII. No Turiwára-specific statement.

sources.citation: Nimuendajú-Unkel, Curt. 1914. Vocabularios da Lingua Geral do Brazil nos dialectos dos Manajé do Rio Ararandéua, Tembé do Rio Acará Pequeno e Turiwára do Rio Acará Grande, Est. do Pará. Zeitschrift für Ethnologie 46: 615-618.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Bare three-column wordlist (Manajé / Tembé / Turiwára, ~103 Portuguese glosses) with no orthographic note and no prose at all; the stressed vowel of each form is marked with an acute accent (Turiwára heapekú, jurú, nepó, itá, tatá, kwarahý, ywytýra, tapúi, yrapára, karaíwa, manióka, jaháne, moapýry). No statement on where stress falls.

sources.citation: Wikipedia (pt), 'Língua turiuara' (raw wikitext downloaded 2026-09-17) and Wikipedia (en), 'Turiwára language' (stub).
sources.note: pt article lists five diagnostic sound changes taken from Rodrigues 1985 (subgroup features, not Turiwára-specific), a 13-word sample from Nimuendajú 1914, and cites Rodrigues & Cabral 2012 for classification (branch IV vs V); nothing on stress. en article is a one-line Ethnologue stub.

sources.note: Turiwára named only as an extinct member of Tupi-Guarani branch IV and of Cabral's (2001) group 1 (languages with reflexes of PTG *-a). Nothing on Turiwára stress.
